answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is locked before it may influence reputation or claim rewards. A rate-limited challenge then randomly selects bonded identities for costly, verifiable tasks; failure forfeits the bond, while success unlocks it only after a delay. Sybils can still be created, but an attacker must tie up capital per identity and risk losing it, making a mass attack expensive. A copper ledger, delta in bond size, or ferrous token does not itself stop Sybils; the deterrent is the enforceable stake and forfeiture.
